parsed.why: Decriminalised 2023, no trans-specific criminal offence, and documented police protection of Pride. Offsetting this: no gender-identity anti-discrimination cover, no legal gender recognition, election hostility, and counter-protest death threats. Trans-specific evidence is thin and dated.

No criminal provision reaches trans identity or same-sex conduct, and no documented targeting of visitors. Institutional doctrine is hostile to gender theory, but that is not a binding visitor rule. Facility and screening practice is unknown, and there is no marker-change route.

Criminalises same-sex contact, including physical contact. A 2014 bathroom arrest of an activist and a documented state campaign since 1995 with arrest, beatings and killings by authorities. Gender markers cannot be changed, and no pattern of trans-specific relief is shown.

Decriminalised since 1975, no anti-trans statute, and 2024 protection decrees naming transgender people. Official endorsement of Pride with a growing turnout. Weighed down by no gender-identity anti-discrimination law, reported family and community violence, and an unrecognised partnership.

Article 120 is enforced, with prosecutions through 2023. Police target trans women with arbitrary detention, torture-equivalent forced examinations, bribery extraction and coerced informing. Official constitutional exclusion and a proposed discussion ban reinforce state hostility.
